subtitle: What classical forecasting models quietly assume

steps.label: Stationary
steps.sub: Constant mean/variance, dependence by lag only

steps.label: Trend or seasonality
steps.sub: Breaks stationarity -- mean shifts with time

code:
noise      ADF stat -17.00  p = 0.000  (stationary)
walk       ADF stat  -1.95  p = 0.307  (not stationary)
walk diff  ADF stat -17.04  p = 0.000  (stationary)

# ADF null: non-stationary | KPSS null: stationary
caption: Differencing the random walk made it stationary

code:
random walk:  0.97, 0.95, 0.92 ...  (slow decay)
white noise:  0.01, -0.04, 0.07 ... (near zero)
caption: Slow ACF decay signals trend; near-zero ACF signals noise

code:
sales ADF p: 0.999   (cannot reject non-stationary)
sales KPSS p: 0.01   (reject stationary)

# both tests agree: NOT stationary
caption: Trend + seasonality from Lesson 6 -- exactly what the tests are built to catch

code:
d1    = s.diff().dropna()           # removes trend
d1_12 = s.diff().diff(12).dropna()  # removes season too

# after d1 only:  ACF lag 12 = 0.70  (season still there!)
# after d1 + d12: ACF lag 12 = -0.31 (season gone)
caption: ADF said "stationary" after one difference -- the ACF plot caught what the test missed
